summary: Adversarial source audit of the six-colour chain; no compute. ARROW 1 (ternary -> |P|<=2) is machine-checked as palette_triple_null -> palette_cardinality (BinaryPalettes.lean:252,260), but both are Fin 5 and the proof needs the complement of the 3-set to be a PAIR (Finset.card_eq_two :256) plus ae_not_binary_circle :258. At k=6 the complement is a triple, so the proof cannot transfer even though the arrow's SHAPE is k-insensitive. Five consumers named. ARROW 2: Prop 7.1 is stated for l in {3,4,5}; consumer fullApprox_exists {c : C -> Fin 5} (FullApproximation.lean:330). The alpha threshold is located exactly: Lemma 7.4 (COMPRESSED-PROOF:986) has denominator >= 1 - 5*alpha > 0, so the condition is alpha < 1/k, i.e. arithmetic not geometry; at k=6 it is 1/6 and every downstream constant needs re-derivation. ARROW 3: the finite objects are Fin 5 / Fin 4->Bool, decide-verified (Exclusion.lean:17-24, Interfaces.lean:19-37); no 6-cycle counterpart exists. ARROW 4 is genuinely k-generic, so conditional on arrow 1 it is free. CONCLUSION: two arrows are blocked by their proofs, not their statements; ternary exclusion at k=6 does NOT give chi>=7. Three missing lemmas named with consuming declarations; one falsifying instance narrowed to the centre-dependent class. Packet banked, not run.

verified_results.statement: Arrow 1 is a machine-checked implication palette_triple_null (BinaryPalettes.lean:252) -> palette_cardinality (:260), both Fin 5, the latter concluding 1 <= |P| and |P| <= 2; its five consumers are Exclusion.lean:130, Interfaces.lean:78, States.lean:319, Accumulation.lean:161 and :361.
verified_results.grade: computational (machine-checked in the tree); consumer list from grep, not from any summary

verified_results.statement: The proof of palette_triple_null cannot transfer to k=6: it computes (univ \ S).card = 2 (:255), applies Finset.card_eq_two (:256) and invokes ae_not_binary_circle (:258), a TWO-label statement. At k=6 the complement of a 3-set has 3 elements, so both decisive steps fail. The arrow's shape (exclude |P|>=3 -> |P|<=2) is nonetheless k-insensitive.
verified_results.grade: paper-reviewed + computational (source reading of the proof body)

verified_results.statement: Alpha threshold located exactly: Lemma 7.4 (COMPRESSED-PROOF:986) requires 0 < alpha < 1/5 because its normalisation has denominator >= 1 - 5*alpha > 0, and targets the complete graph on five vertices. Hence the condition is alpha < 1/k, i.e. alpha < 1/6 at k=6, and all downstream constants (mesh <= 2, rho, eps_n) must be re-derived for the smaller alpha.
verified_results.grade: paper-reviewed (the compression states it); the 1/k reading is my own arithmetic

verified_results.statement: Proposition 7.1 is stated for l in {3,4,5} only, and the tree's consumer fullApprox_exists is hard-wired to Fin 5 (FullApproximation.lean:330, finite-core variant :268). There is no l=6 argument anywhere in the sources.

Arrow 3's finite objects are k=5-specific and decide-verified: Exclusion.lean:17-24 (five_admissible_diag, five_diag_disjoint/nonempty/unique, five_adj_four, five_no_common_adj) on Fin 5, and Interfaces.lean:19-37 (interface_four_*) on Fin 4 -> Bool. A 6-cycle interface has no counterpart, and the paper's length-4 and length-5 exclusion arguments use devices (a two-diagonal parity rule; a one-positive-one-negative sign run) that do not extend to length 6.

Arrow 4 is genuinely k-generic: Lemma 7.5 (COMPRESSED-PROOF:997) needs only multiplicity <= 2 and mesh <= 2, and PlanarCover.compact_open_cover_impossible (PlanarCovers.lean:374) is proved for a general constant R. Conditional on arrow 1 supplying |P| <= 2, this arrow costs nothing extra.
verified_results.grade: computational (from a prior audit of the topology section; not re-verified this block)

verified_results.statement: Conclusion: two of the four arrows are blocked by their PROOFS rather than their statements; ternary exclusion at k=6 would give |P| <= 2 but does NOT give chi >= 7, since L2, L3 and the alpha < 1/6 constants pass are still required, together with the independent local-finiteness hypothesis (W) of section 7.
verified_results.grade: proposed (my synthesis; each ingredient graded above)

verified_results.statement: L1 (highest value): palette_triple_null at Fin 6, consuming a Fin 6 palette_cardinality. Its statement already transfers; only the proof is missing.

L2: the l=6 case of Proposition 7.1 at alpha < 1/6, consuming a Fin 6 fullApprox_exists. L3: the l=6 common-interface cycle exclusion, consuming the k=6 analogue of the five_* / interface_four_* layer.

Proposed falsifying instance for L1: a measurable weak 6-colouring with a 3-set inside a palette on a positive-measure direction set. It must be CENTRE-DEPENDENT, because on a centre-independent field the record's unit-triangle bound gives 3|P| <= 6, i.e. |P| <= 2, which is why the 36-sector ternary word was withdrawn. Not constructed.
verified_results.grade: proposed, unconstructed; the centre-dependence narrowing is paper-reviewed

verified_results.statement: Exact SAT-relaxation constraints read from the record with their labels: (5.2) colouring axiom, (5.3) two-centre transport, (5.7) sixty-degree exclusion P_x(f) cap P_x(Rf) = empty, Lemma 6.2 / (6.2) cycle edge exclusions, Lemma 5.5 binary-centre separation, (8.4) region inequality; the record's own verdict is that (T), (SA), (5.2), (5.7) are satisfiable at every cycle length and that no palette axiom proves (W) at k=6 without proving the problem.
verified_results.grade: paper-reviewed (the record's findings, which I did not re-derive)

verified_results.statement: The source-only witness-combination packet is banked unchanged (combine/combine_witnesses.py, fixtures.json, README.md); no benchmark was run and the closed seed was not rerun.
verified_results.grade: status statement; the packet was syntax-checked only, one block earlier

conjectures: L1 is plausibly the only genuinely hard arrow: arrows 2-4 look like a finite re-computation plus a constants pass once a k=6 ternary exclusion exists, whereas L1's existing proof is structurally tied to a two-element complement. If the whole chain is to be extended, L1 is where the effort should go.

Since any falsifier of L1 must be centre-dependent, and the record already shows centre-independent fields admit no ternary palette, the search for a ternary-palette 6-colouring is confined to the same centre-dependent class where (W) is undecided. That coincidence suggests the two questions may be equivalent rather than independent.
